name: AKU SONAM Grad's Heart for Cardiac Care

content.title: AKU SONAM Grad's Heart for Cardiac Care
content.summary: Abraham Mwifa's experience ignited his passion for nursing, shaping his career journey

content.text: One of Abraham Mwifa's most memorable moments occurred during his elective at Aga Khan Hospital, where he was part of a team managing a critically ill patient with Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI). "It was a defining moment, one that reminded me exactly why I chose nursing," recalls the recent graduate of the Post RN-BScN programme. "Seeing the power of interdisciplinary teamwork and realizing that I had something valuable to contribute reinforced my passion for improving cardiac care. It was humbling and inspiring at the same time."
This experience solidified his commitment to nursing and underscored the importance of collaboration and comprehensive patient care.

Abraham's journey at AKU was more than just academic prowess; it was about style of teaching that would shape his perspective as a student. "Evidence-based practice, teamwork, and comprehensive patient care were the pillars of my education here," he explains. "AKU instilled in me a deep sense of curiosity - an urge to keep learning, to adapt, and to embrace change in the ever-evolving field of healthcare."

This mindset has had a profound impact on how he approaches professional growth and patient care, enabling him to stay abreast of the latest advancements and provide the best possible care to his patients.

Abraham acknowledges that balancing academics, clinical rotations, and personal responsibilities was challenging. "There were days when I felt stretched too thin, trying to juggle it all," he admits. "But in those moments, I learned the importance of time management and, more importantly, the value of seeking support."

The AKU faculty, Aga Khan University Hospital staff, his friends, and family played a crucial role in keeping him motivated. Overcoming these challenges made him stronger, more compassionate, and deeply empathetic.

For those considering AKU or pursuing a career in nursing, Abraham offers some advice: "Embrace the journey - the challenges and opportunities alike," he advises. "AKU offers a world-class education, but it demands commitment and resilience. Find a mentor, stay curious, and never lose sight of the fact that nursing is not just a profession... it's a calling. Every day, we have the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in people's lives."

Abraham's aspirations are clear. He wants to use his degree to deliver high-quality, patient-centered care, addressing not just the physical but also the emotional, psychological, and social needs of his patients. He is also passionate about research and hopes to contribute to initiatives that improve patient outcomes. "There are many gaps in healthcare that need addressing, and I hope to contribute to research initiatives that improve patient outcomes," he shares. "But beyond that, I see it as my responsibility to collaborate with other healthcare professionals and raise awareness on preventable diseases within my community."

With his convocation day approaching, Abraham stands at the threshold of a promising future. His time at AKU has equipped him with the knowledge, skills, and resilience to take on the healthcare landscape with confidence. "It's been an incredible journey," he says with a smile. "And it's only just beginning."
